samples.summary: `copyThread` detaches the anchor with `detachYorkieValue`, which this repo documents as broken for Yorkie *array* proxies — and two of the three live anchor shapes carry arrays (`pdf-text.rects`, `docs-range.posRange`). Every `GET /comments`, `PATCH :threadId` and `POST :threadId/replies` response for a PDF or docs document created in the editor will therefore return CRDT metadata in place of those arrays.
samples.evidence: `packages/backend/src/yorkie/yorkie-json.ts:13-20` states outright that `detachYorkieValue` "branches on `Array.isArray`, which is false for a Yorkie array proxy, so a chart's `seriesColumns` or a slide's `elements` would come back as `{createdAt, movedAt}` CRDT metadata" — and `comment-ops.ts`'s own `isThread` docblock repeats the same fact. The anchors that reach `copyThread` do contain arrays: `packages/frontend/src/app/files/comments/pdf-comment-store.ts:61` stores `rects: Array.from(anchor.rects ?? []).map(copyRect)` for a `pdf-text` anchor (and deliberately uses `Array.from` rather than a spread "because a spread would carry live proxy objects out of the CRDT"); `packages/frontend/src/types/comments.ts:31` types a docs anchor's `posRange` as `TreePosStructRange`, a two-element tuple. `comments.controller.ts` returns `copyThread` output straight to the client for every doc/pdf thread it did not itself create. The comment-ops docblock even cites `pdf-comment-store.ts`'s field-by-field `copyAnchor` as the bug being avoided, while choosing the one helper that reintroduces it for arrays.

samples.summary: `docs/design/rest-api.md` is the top-level document that enumerates the v1 route table and the controller file tree; it still describes the pre-change surface. None of the new route families are listed (tab delete / `:tabId/reorder` / `:tabId/duplicate`, `tabs/:tabId/images`, `slides` + `layouts`, `comments`, board `content`), and the file tree at ~line 564-568 omits `comments.controller.ts`, `slides.controller.ts` and `worksheet-images.controller.ts`.
samples.evidence: docs/design/rest-api.md:198-200 lists only list/create/rename for tabs; :255 documents `POST /api/v1/.../tabs/:tid/move` as the row/column axis move — the very route that forced the new tab reorder onto `/reorder` — with no mention of the new verb; :564-568 lists `tabs.controller.ts` and `images.controller.ts` but none of the three controllers this change adds. Grep for `documents/:documentId/tabs` and `comments` across docs/design returned no entry for any new route.

samples.summary: `duplicateTab` rebuilds `TabMeta` field by field and copies only `kind`, `datasourceId` and `query`, silently dropping every other optional field the type carries (`lakehouseSourceId`, `lakehouseRef`, `asOf`). A future sheet-tab field added to `TabMeta` is dropped by the copy with no compile error, and if a `lakehouse`/`datasource` tab ever gains a `sheets` entry the copy becomes a tab the viewer cannot resolve.
samples.evidence: `packages/frontend/src/app/spreadsheet/lakehouse-view.tsx:74` reads `tab?.lakehouseSourceId` and bails without it; `packages/frontend/src/app/documents/lakehouse-tab.ts:27-28` sets `lakehouseSourceId` and `lakehouseRef` on the meta. Today the path is unreachable because `tabs.controller.ts:255` refuses a tab with no worksheet and lakehouse/datasource tabs have none, so this is latent rather than broken — but the whitelist is silent, not typed.

samples.summary: The backend's new `applySetResolved` documents that Yorkie's object proxy throws `fail to find <key>` when `delete` targets a key that was never set, and guards its two deletes accordingly. Its frontend twin, which writes the same worksheet thread map, still deletes `resolvedAt`/`resolvedBy` unguarded — so a thread created (and never resolved) through the new API and then reopened by the editor would throw there.
samples.evidence: packages/frontend/src/app/spreadsheet/yorkie-worksheet-comments.ts:141-144 does `delete t.resolvedAt; delete t.resolvedBy;` with no presence check, versus the guarded form added in packages/backend/src/yorkie/comment-ops.ts (`applySetResolved`). Reachability depends on the UI ever calling reopen on an unresolved thread, which I could not confirm.

verdict.reason: Verified independently. copyThread detaches the anchor with detachYorkieValue (comment-ops.ts:99), and detachYorkieValue branches on Array.isArray (yorkie-json.ts:172), which this repo states four separate times is false for a Yorkie array proxy and yields {createdAt,movedAt} CRDT metadata (yorkie-json.ts:13-20, worksheet-charts.controller.ts:63-66, worksheet-filter-pivot.controller.ts:65-70, lessons file 11-23), backed by a real-yorkie.Document regression suite (worksheet-filter-pivot.controller.spec.ts:88-144). The editor-created anchors that reach copyThread do carry arrays: pdf-text `rects: PdfRect[]` (types/comments.ts:66-71, pdf-comment-store.ts:56-64) and docs-range `posRange` written as a Yorkie array (yorkie-comment-store.ts:180-187, with 81-88 explaining it is left as a proxy on purpose). The path is live and unguarded: GET calls listThreads(doc.getRoot().comments) on an attached document (comments.controller.ts:250-257, yorkie.service.ts:46-57) and PATCH/replies return copyThread from inside doc.update (comments.controller.ts:599, 403). The only anchor test uses a plain-object pdf-region anchor (comment-ops.spec.ts:263-281), so it cannot catch the proxy case. This is a cross-module contract violation (a helper documented as unsafe for array-bearing shapes applied to data whose shape is owned by other modules), not something visible from the diff alone, and it silently returns wrong data on a reachable API path.

finding.summary: `duplicateTab` copies the worksheet verbatim, so the copy's charts (and its `pivotTable`) still carry `sourceTabId` pointing at the ORIGINAL tab. `chart-utils.ts` resolves chart data with `root.sheets[chart.sourceTabId]`, so every chart on the duplicated tab renders the source tab's numbers, not the copy's — and a duplicated pivot output tab silently becomes a second dependent that makes the new `resolveDelete` refuse to delete the source tab, naming a tab the user never configured.
finding.evidence: packages/frontend/src/app/spreadsheet/chart-utils.ts:116 `const sourceSheet = root.sheets[chart.sourceTabId];` (same at :188 and :281), and packages/frontend/src/app/spreadsheet/pivot/use-pivot-table.ts:135 `const sourceWs = root.sheets[definition.sourceTabId];`. The new duplicate writes `const copy: Worksheet = { ...worksheet, comments: {} }` (packages/backend/src/yorkie/tab-ops.ts, duplicateTab) — chart ids and `sourceTabId`/`pivotTable.sourceTabId` are not remapped to the new tab id. Fix belongs in `duplicateTab`.

verdict.reason: All quoted evidence verified in the repository. tab-ops.ts:167 `const copy: Worksheet = { ...worksheet, comments: {} }` copies the worksheet verbatim except comments; the Worksheet type (worksheet-document.ts:88-99) includes `charts` and `pivotTable`, both of which carry a `sourceTabId` that is not remapped to `newTabId`. Editor-created charts stamp `sourceTabId: tabId` (sheet-view.tsx:421), so the invariant that a chart's source is its own tab holds for editor content and is broken by the copy. Consumers outside the diff resolve data straight through that field: chart-utils.ts:116, :188, :281 (`root.sheets[chart.sourceTabId]`) and use-pivot-table.ts:135 (`root.sheets[definition.sourceTabId]`), so the duplicate's charts render the ORIGINAL tab's data and never reflect edits to the copy. The pivot consequence is also real: resolveDelete (tab-ops.ts:85-92) and the editor's equivalent scans (document-detail.tsx:515, :555) enumerate every tab whose pivotTable.sourceTabId matches, so a duplicated pivot output tab becomes an extra unconfigured dependent blocking deletion of the source. No remapping occurs upstream — tabs.controller.ts:255-266 only unwrapJson's the worksheet and passes it through — and tab-ops.spec.ts:178-213 asserts only naming/order/cells/comment-stripping, confirming no remap exists. Reachable via the live duplicate endpoint (cli/src/commands/tabs.ts:196). In-lane as a violated invariant that modules outside the diff read; major impact (wrong results rendered, silent extra dependency).

finding.summary: `copyThread` detaches the anchor with the generic `detachYorkieValue`, but a docs-range anchor's `posRange` is explicitly documented as a value that does not survive a generic detach. `GET /comments` on a `doc` document therefore returns a `posRange` made of Yorkie CRDT metadata instead of a usable `TreePosStructRange`, so an API consumer cannot resolve or round-trip a docs thread anchor.
finding.evidence: packages/frontend/src/app/docs/comments/yorkie-comment-store.ts:81-88 states the invariant: "`posRange` is deliberately left as-is. Stored as a Yorkie array, its `toJSON()` returns a string-escaped serialization that does not round-trip through `JSON.parse(JSON.stringify(...))`" — and this branch's own `yorkie-json.ts:13-20` warns that `detachYorkieValue` branches on `Array.isArray`, which is false for a Yorkie array proxy, so it returns `{createdAt, movedAt}` metadata. `copyThread` uses exactly that helper on `t.anchor`, and the comments controller's `list`/`setResolved`/`reply` return its output for `doc` documents.

verdict.reason: Verified independently. `copyThread` detaches the anchor with the generic walker at packages/backend/src/yorkie/comment-ops.ts:99, and `detachYorkieValue` branches on `Array.isArray` (packages/backend/src/yorkie/yorkie-json.ts:172) before falling into an `Object.entries` object walk (yorkie-json.ts:180-185) — which the repository itself documents as producing `{createdAt, movedAt}` CRDT metadata for a Yorkie array proxy (yorkie-json.ts:13-20, worksheet-charts.controller.ts:63-65, worksheet-filter-pivot.controller.ts:65-69), and comment-ops.ts:112-123 independently confirms `Array.isArray` is false for values stored in the CRDT. A docs-range anchor's `posRange` is exactly such an array value: typed `TreePosStructRange` (frontend/src/types/comments.ts:28-33), written nested inside the anchor object at yorkie-comment-store.ts:180-187, destructured as an array by the only consumer `resolveDocsAnchor` (docs-anchor.ts:120), and deliberately excluded from any generic detach by the store's documented invariant (yorkie-comment-store.ts:81-88). The path is reachable: `doc` is commentable (comments.controller.ts:60), only POST is refused for docs (comments.controller.ts:276-289), while `list` returns `listThreads(doc.getRoot().comments)` (comments.controller.ts:250-257) and `mutateThread` returns `copyThread(thread)` for reply/resolve (comments.controller.ts:599) over a live SDK Document proxy (yorkie.service.ts:36-57). No guard special-cases docs anchors — the only anchor post-processing, `withSref`, returns early for anything that is not `sheet-cell` (comments.controller.ts:703-714) — and no test covers a proxied `posRange` (comment-ops.spec.ts:20-121). So GET/PATCH/reply on a doc document emits an unusable anchor; the invariant belongs to another module, so it is in this lens's lane and is not refutable as not-present, already-guarded, or out-of-scope.
